generic_sampling_rules.build_order: Finalize each table completely before its dependents: (1) sample free columns, (2) apply per-column exceptions/forced literals, (3) sample fresh PK/UNIQUE values, (4) deduplicate unique tuples, (5) apply group-size/tie targets, (6) apply semantic rules that touch non-key columns only, (7) apply null rule, (8) MATERIALIZE immutable final key tuple set. Children then sample FKs exclusively from the parent's materialized final key tuples. No parent-side mutation may occur after child FK fill; if a parent is ever touched post-hoc, re-run child FK fill.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_pk: Sequential unique integers within [1, 230]; never NULL. For PKs that are also FKs (Students.student_id, Candidates.candidate_id), values are taken exclusively from the parent's materialized key pool (copied), never generated fresh.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_fk: Sample from the parent table's MATERIALIZED final key tuples (after dedup, group-size, tie, semantic and null rules); coerce to child's declared type (VARCHAR parent -> INTEGER child via CAST); never NULL for NOT NULL FK columns; fail loudly if parent pool is empty.
generic_sampling_rules.composite_fk: Sample the joint tuple from the parent's MATERIALIZED final composite key tuples; never sample composite-FK columns independently.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_measure_or_flag: Random integer in observed range; flags drawn from {0,1}.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_name_or_text: Random word string length 3-30 using letters/spaces; near-variants (case changes) inserted when an equality/LIKE pattern is targeted.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_phone: Random phone format matching observed styles (digits, parens, x-extension, dots, hyphens).
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_char_small: Random short uppercase letter string length 1-3 within CHAR length.
generic_sampling_rules.literal_injection: For every per_column_exceptions entry with explicit numeric 'values' on a NON-FK column, force at least one generated row per listed literal and one step on each side of each numeric boundary. For entries listed as 'inject_into_parent', inject the literal into the PARENT primary key stream before the parent is finalized; children then FK-fill from the parent's final set. FK columns are never force-overwritten with values outside the parent's final key set.
generic_sampling_rules.null_rule: Only columns listed in null_targets receive planted NULLs; every other nullable column is always non-NULL. Each null_target column gets at least one NULL per instance and a share matching spec_share (compact database's share, default 0.10-0.20 when unknown). NOT NULL/PK/FK/UNIQUE columns never get NULL. Planted NULLs are never replaced.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback: all 20 instances invalid with new_integrity_failures; 2388 FK violations total. Dominant: Student_Course_Attendance.(student_id,course_id) -> Student_Course_Registrations.(student_id,course_id) with 2275 rows across 20 instances; also Student_Course_Registrations.course_id -> Courses.course_id with 113 rows across 11 instances. In instance.py, fill_foreign_keys_consistently draws each FK child column independently from the parent column's values (rng.choice per column). For the composite FK (student_id, course_id) this produces pairs that were never registered together, so the composite FK is violated. Similarly, Student_Course_Registrations.course_id is drawn from Courses.course_id values, but the sampler for course_id (INTEGER) can produce values not present in Courses (Courses.course_id is VARCHAR(100) and the FK target values are strings), and the writer disables foreign_keys pragma so violations are silently committed.
issues.requested_revision: Make FK generation respect composite keys: for a multi-column FK, sample whole parent tuples (from the parent table's generated+compact rows) and assign them jointly to the child columns, not column-by-column. Also ensure the child column's sampler domain is restricted to the parent's actual key values (including type coercion for VARCHAR vs INTEGER course_id), and/or re-enable foreign_keys enforcement in the writer so violations are caught rather than silently written. Re-run and confirm new_fk_violations = 0 for all instances.

issues.evidence: Student_Course_Attendance has PRIMARY KEY (student_id, course_id) and FK to Student_Course_Registrations on the same pair. Because fill_foreign_keys_consistently samples student_id and course_id independently, the generated attendance rows also frequently duplicate the (student_id, course_id) PK across rows (the PK dedup in sample_fresh_primary_keys runs before FK fill in build_random_instance, so FK-filled columns are not re-deduplicated). The feedback shows 0 new_duplicate_keys only because the writer's executemany fails and falls back to per-row inserts that skip duplicates — but the FK violations remain. This is a latent correctness gap: the PK dedup step is applied to the pre-FK columns, then FK columns are overwritten afterwards.
issues.requested_revision: Apply primary-key deduplication after FK columns are filled (or fill FKs before dedup), and for composite FKs sample joint parent tuples so the resulting (student_id, course_id) pairs are both unique and valid registrations.

issues.evidence: The generation specification is empty ({}), so there is no documented statement of the value domains, sampling rules, NULL rule, or FK-consistency requirement that the program is supposed to implement. issues.evidence: Execution feedback reports 2388 FK violations across all 20 instances (0 valid). The largest source is Student_Course_Attendance.(student_id,course_id) -> Student_Course_Registrations.(student_id,course_id): 2275 rows in 20/20 instances; plus Student_Course_Registrations.course_id -> Courses.course_id: 113 rows in 11 instances. Root causes in code: (1) In instance.py, `fill_foreign_keys_consistently` samples each FK column independently (`out[cm.name] = [rng.choice(pv) ...]`), so the composite FK (student_id,course_id) into Student_Course_Registrations is filled column-by-column, not by joint parent tuples - violating the spec dependency 'sample joint parent tuples; do not sample child columns independently'. (2) `sample_fresh_primary_keys`/`drop_unique_duplicates` and `_apply_null_rule` run AFTER FK fill and can drop/alter parent tuples the child referenced; but more decisively the child attendance rows only draw from parents present in the generated dict `inst` (which only holds generated parent values) — packed rows / later-filtered rows become orphan parents. (3) Courses.course_id is VARCHAR and Student_Course_Registrations.course_id is INTEGER; the spec requires 'CAST(Courses.course_id AS INTEGER)'; the code raw-samples the string pool (`rng.choice(pv)`), so FK values are string-typed against an INTEGER FK column, and when parent PK dedup drops generated Courses rows, child course_id values link to non-existent courses.
issues.requested_revision: Implement the composite-FK joint-tuple sampling explicitly (register the FK as a tuple (student_id,course_id) and sample whole parent tuples), perform the composite-FK fill for Student_Course_Attendance from the MATERIALIZED final Student_Course_Registrations tuples (after dedup and null-rule, not the transient dict), and coerce Course FK values via CAST(Courses.course_id AS INTEGER) both in the parent sampling and the child fill. Then re-run and require new_fk_violations == 0 for all instances.

issues.evidence: Spec nullable-column rules (eight-point note and program generic_sampling_rules) forbid NULL in NOT NULL columns. Although not_null_violations is 0 in the executed run, the mechanism is fragile: instance.py `fill_foreign_keys_consistently` returns `[None]*n` when a parent table has no values (`pv` empty), and _apply_null_rule is later applied uniformly to all nullable columns regardless of whether they are FK columns. For Parents used by Student_Course_Registrations.course_id (Courses.course_id is VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL, PK) the PK-sampling path can also produce NULL via filtering (`cols = _filter(...)`) but the only mechanism preventing NOT NULL failure today is SQLite's DDL check. The spec's NULL-target list explicitly names 'Students.student_id, Student_Course_Attendance.student_id, Candidate_Assessments.candidate_id' as NOT NULL columns and 'never NULL', contradicting the null_targets semantics (these are NOT NULL PK columns).
issues.requested_revision: Fix the spec null_targets field to list nullable columns only (e.g., People.middle_name, People_Addresses.date_to, Students.student_details, etc.), and in the engineer code ensure _apply_null_rule never introduces NULL into a column with column_meta.notnull or pk_pos>0 (currently guarded, but also guard FK fill fallback pv-empty path: fail loudly rather than emitting NULLs).

issues.evidence: Execution feedback: every one of 20 instances is invalid with `new_integrity_failures`; aggregate `fk_violations: 322`. Largest offender is `Student_Course_Attendance.(student_id,course_id) -> Student_Course_Registrations.(student_id,course_id)` with 304 violating rows across all 20 instances, plus `Student_Course_Registrations.course_id -> Courses.course_id` (10 rows/5 instances), `Students.student_id -> People.person_id` (6/5) and `Candidates.candidate_id -> People.person_id` (2/2).
issues.requested_revision: Fix the FK pipeline so generated rows never introduce FK violations. Root cause: in `instance.py::build_random_instance`, `fill_foreign_keys_consistently` / `_fill_composite_fk` sample parent values from `instance.get(pt, ...)` (the *pre-dedup, pre-NULL* row set assembled by the samplers) and from `schema.original_values`, but afterwards `sample_fresh_primary_keys`, `drop_unique_duplicates`, `_apply_group_size_target`, `_apply_tie_target`, `_apply_semantic_rules` and `_apply_null_rule` can rewrite or delete parent key rows (`course_id` resequenced by the group-size target, `student_id`/`candidate_id` rewritten by `_apply_semantic_rules`, and `Students.student_id`/`Candidates.candidate_id`/`Student_Course_Registrations.course_id` can be dropped by dedup). Children therefore reference parent keys that no longer exist in the materialized final table. The spec explicitly requires sampling (including the composite FK) from the *MATERIALIZED final parent rows after dedup and null-rule*. Reorder/rebuild: fully finalize each parent table (dedup, group-size, tie, semantic and null rules applied) and materialize its final key set, then sample all child FKs from that final set, and re-verify by running PRAGMA foreign_key_check on each written unit before `os.replace`.

issues.evidence: `instance.py::_apply_null_rule` iterates `for cm in tm.columns` and never consults `spec.NULL_TARGETS`; because the spec's `null_targets` list is effectively unused, the NULL share is instead computed from `schema.original_values` using `share = ... if ov else 0.2`. Feedback shows non-target nullable columns receiving NULLs: `Addresses.line_1: NULL 2 / 48`, `People.first_name: NULL 3 / 63`, `People.last_name: NULL 5 / 63`, `People_Addresses.date_from: NULL 5 / 67`, and `Courses.other_details: NULL 101 / 101` (every generated course has NULL other_details).
issues.requested_revision: Drive the NULL rule from `spec.NULL_TARGETS` (nullable columns only) rather than from every nullable column, and ensure the share matches the compact share for that column. The generic rule to force a NULL into `line_1`, `first_name`, `last_name` and `date_from` overrides designer intent and can distort query-result variation for queries targeting those columns; `Courses.other_details` at 100% NULL is not a 'share following the compact database'. At minimum, skip forcing NULLs on columns not in `NULL_TARGETS`, or align the fallback share with observed compact shares per column.

issues.evidence: Specification `per_column_exceptions` asserts `Students.student_id comparison_boundary values [170,171,172]`, `Student_Course_Registrations.course_id comparison_boundary [300,301,302]`, `Student_Course_Attendance.student_id [170,171,172]`, `Student_Course_Attendance.course_id [300,301,302]`, and `Courses.course_name/description = 'statistics'/'STATISTICS'`. But the schema has `Student_Course_Registrations.course_id -> Courses.course_id` (VARCHAR PK, values '301'..'308' per spec) and `Students.student_id -> People.person_id`; injecting child `course_id` values 300/301/302 and `student_id` 170/171/172 requires those exact parent keys to exist, yet the spec's `Courses.course_id` compact domain is only 301–308 and People keys are generated from sequential ints. `Student_Course_Registrations.course_id` is also a NOT NULL FK, so literal injection either forces `_fill_foreign_keys_consistently` to be overridden by the forced values (causing FK violations) or forces those forced literals to be dropped (defeating the boundary target). The current code does both: `_inject_forced_values` runs before FK fill for non-FK columns, but `Student_Course_Registrations.course_id` is an FK, so the forced values overwrite FK-consistent values and then must be re-repaired — there is no such repair in the code.
issues.requested_revision: Decide the interaction between `forced literal injection` and FK consistency. Either (a) drop boundary literals on FK child columns (`Student_Course_Registrations.course_id`, `Student_Course_Attendance.student_id`, `Student_Course_Attendance.course_id`) since the parent's materialized key set cannot contain 300 without the parent having it — and extend the parent `Courses.course_id` literal domain to include 300 if 300-adjacency is needed, or (b) explicitly specify that `Students.student_id`, `Student_Course_Registrations.course_id`, `Student_Course_Attendance.student_id/course_id` are *derived* from FK fill and boundary variation on those columns is only reachable if the parent holds the boundary values, and then update the spec table sizes / `FORCED_VALUES` to inject those boundary keys into the parents instead of into the children. Current state is internally contradictory and yields FK violations.

issues.evidence: `instance.py::_apply_semantic_rules` rewrites primary keys (`Students.student_id` and `Candidates.candidate_id` if `<= 0`) *after* child FKs were sampled; and the parent-key pruning in `sample_fresh_primary_keys`/`drop_unique_duplicates` also runs after FK fill. Neither is followed by a re-sample of children. Feedback's `Students.student_id -> People.person_id` violations (6 rows, 5 instances) and `Candidates.candidate_id -> People.person_id` violations (2 rows, 2 instances) are explained by `_parent_pool` including the original compact `People.person_id` values that get dropped/mutated by the later parent-side dedup/semantic rules.
issues.requested_revision: Function `_apply_semantic_rules` must not touch primary-key columns, or must run before FK sampling, and final parent key sets must be immutable once child FKs are sampled. Same for `drop_unique_duplicates` on unique/PK columns. Any post-hoc parent mutation must trigger *re-sampling* of dependent children (a two-pass build: finalize parents first, then children).

issues.evidence: The 'unmatched_join_rows / parent_rows_without_children' target, per spec, is a pattern that must be observable, not explicitly forbidden. But the current pipeline for e.g. `Students.student_id` first builds Students with FK-derived keys from People, then `sample_fresh_primary_keys` dedups on Student keys, then `_apply_semantic_rules` is run — and `Students.student_id` can never be a value that isn't also in People, so 'unmatched join rows' on `Students.student_id -> People.person_id` is not directly reachable; separately, the composite FK fill samples from *all* materialized registration rows, including those without attendance, so Attendance has extra rows and `parent_rows_without_children` for `Student_Course_Registrations -> Student_Course_Attendance` *is* reachable, but the FK integrity requirement blocks it. The round report does not report any per-target reachability failures separately; instead the units are all rejected on FK violations before the target checks can be read.
issues.requested_revision: Resolve the tension between the spec's `parent_rows_without_children` targets and FK integrity. If unmatched join patterns are intended, they must be on joins like `Students -> Student_Course_Registrations` (child row does not exist) — which is legal — and not on `Students.student_id -> People.person_id` (a NOT NULL FK that is physically impossible to violate while satisfying integrity). The spec's `Students.student_id unmatched_join_rows joins_with People_Addresses.person_id` is reachable (a student need not have an address), but this should be clarified so the FK-violation-driven failure is not blamed on the target.

issues.evidence: `Students.student_id -> People.person_id` and `Candidates.candidate_id -> People.person_id` are both FK constraints. The spec lists `Students.student_id` as a `comparison_boundary` target with values [170,171,172] and `Candidates.candidate_id` as `unmatched_join_rows` target — but generating a boundary/fresh student_id that is not in People directly causes an FK violation. Since `Students.student_id` is also the FK to People, its values can only be a subset of People's final key set; a fresh number like 171 must exist in People for the boundary to be legal. Spec's generic rule 'integer_fk: sample from parent materialized final key values' is thus under-specified for the boundary case: it must say 'inject the boundary into the parent's key set, then propagate' or explicitly drop the boundary target.
issues.requested_revision: Either (i) remove `Students.student_id` and `Candidates.candidate_id` from `per_column_exceptions` boundary/unmatched targets (they are FK columns and boundary values are not freely choosable), or (ii) add a spec rule 'for boundary values on FK columns, inject the boundary into the parent primary key stream before finalizing the parent, then FK-fill children' with a matching code path. Also remove or rename `Students.student_id unmatched_join_rows joins_with [... "People_Addresses.person_id"]` since it is semantically meaningless (a person_id present only in People_Addresses does not imply a Student).

issues.evidence: `spec.TABLE_SIZES` uses fixed near-constant per-table sizes but `choose_table_sizes` adds `rng.randint(-2,2)` for every table independently. The spec table `Student_Course_Registrations: 30` and `Student_Course_Attendance: 30` yields (via the feedback's row counts of ~100-124 rows added) that attendance has far fewer rows than registrations or vice versa. This does not itself cause the observed FK violation, but it makes the `group_sizes: 1, 2 and >=3` target very brittle: `_apply_group_size_target` allocates only 1+2+3=6 rows to size groups, which is unlikely to hold once `rng.shuffle` runs across 30 rows with `rng.choice(pool)` overwriting them.
issues.requested_revision: Make the group-size target deterministic: reserve dedicated row indices for each group size, or assign distinct course_ids with counts matching 1,2,>=3 after FK fill; do not `shuffle` the whole sequence into other random draws. Also verify the tie target (`_apply_tie_target` sets index 1 only, using `base = cols[col][0]`, so if index 0 is NULL it silently no-ops) — log per-instance target achievement in `run_report`.

Execution feedback does not report tie-target success rate.
Reproducibility of target achievement across seeds: the reported run is for one seed-base; the spec promises reachability — no per-instance target audit is included in the execution feedback.

Whether the `Courses.course_id` VARCHAR coherence with `Student_Course_Registrations.course_id` INTEGER is preserved after `_apply_semantic_rules`' positive-integer fixup (which can rewrite course_id to a random 301-308, potentially colliding with the composite PK after registration dedup; PK-duplicate count in feedback is 0, but this only inspected final rows).

issues.evidence: All 20 instances fail with RuntimeError('foreign_key_check failed: N violations') at tscore_gen/writer.py:66. The program reports n_ok 0, n_fail 20, and zero instance directories are written. This is a hard blocker: no instance is produced at all.
issues.requested_revision: Diagnose and fix the FK violations. The most likely cause is that the compact database is copied verbatim (shutil.copyfile(orig, part)) and generated rows are appended, but the generated FK values are drawn from a pool that mixes generated parent keys with compact parent keys via _parent_pool/_parent_tuples. If the compact DB already contains rows that violate FKs (or if generated child rows reference compact parent keys that are not actually present in the copied DB, e.g. because schema.original_values was sampled/truncated or because the compact DB's own FK state is inconsistent), foreign_key_check will fail. Verify: (a) whether the compact DB itself passes foreign_key_check before appending; (b) whether _parent_pool's inclusion of schema.original_values (which may be a truncated sample when n > max_rows_per_table) introduces keys not present in the copied DB; (c) whether composite FK sampling from Student_Course_Registrations includes compact rows whose (student_id,course_id) tuples are not actually in the copied DB. The fix must ensure every generated FK value is present in the final written database, and that the compact DB's own integrity is preserved. Do not weaken the foreign_key_check gate; fix the value sourcing.

issues.evidence: In instance.py, _parent_pool and _parent_tuples append schema.original_values (the compact rows read by read_schema) to the generated pool. read_schema samples compact rows when a table exceeds max_rows_per_table (schema.py: 'where rowid %% %d = 0'), so original_values may be a strict subset of the compact DB. Children can then FK-fill to a compact key that was sampled into original_values but is not guaranteed to be in the copied DB — or, conversely, the compact DB may contain parent rows not in original_values. Either way the FK pool is not guaranteed to be a subset of the materialized final parent key set actually written.
issues.requested_revision: Make the FK parent pool exactly the set of parent key tuples that will exist in the written unit: generated parent rows (after finalization) UNION the compact parent rows actually present in the copied DB. Since the compact DB is copied verbatim, the compact parent keys are exactly those in the DB; read them fully (or at least ensure the sampled subset is a subset of what is written, which it is, but the reverse direction — child referencing a compact key not in the DB — must be impossible). Confirm the pool is a subset of the written parent keys and add an assertion before writing.

issues.evidence: The composite FK fill (_fill_composite_fk) samples joint tuples from _parent_tuples, which includes compact Student_Course_Registrations rows. But Student_Course_Attendance's composite FK references Student_Course_Registrations.(student_id,course_id). If the compact DB's Student_Course_Registrations rows are included in the pool but the generated attendance rows are appended to a DB where those compact registration rows exist, that is fine — unless the compact DB itself has attendance rows referencing registrations that were not copied, or the pool includes tuples from original_values that are not in the DB. The 6-14 violations per instance are consistent with a systematic pool/DB mismatch rather than random noise.
issues.requested_revision: After fixing the pool sourcing, re-run and confirm foreign_key_check passes for all instances. Add a per-instance audit that logs which FK (table.column -> parent) produced each violation, so future failures are diagnosable.

issues.evidence: The specification's semantic rules are mostly supported by the compact evidence (date_to >= date_from 8/8; attendance >= min registration date on shown rows; outcome {Pass,Fail}; qualification {A,B,C,D}; course_id numeric 301-306). However, the specification itself flags uncertainty: 'People.middle_name/last_name lengths and near-duplicates unmeasured' and 'attendance rows shown (8) vs registrations (9) suggest sparse attendance'. The tie target on attendance date ('may conflict with sparse attendance sizing') and the boundary injection into People.person_id 170-172 / Courses.course_id 300-310 are assumptions, not measured facts. These are acceptable as uncertain patterns but should be marked as such rather than asserted as evidence-backed rules.
issues.requested_revision: Downgrade the tie target and boundary-injection entries to 'uncertain' in the specification, and note that the attendance-date tie may be unreachable under the chosen table sizes. This does not block generation but should be recorded so the engineer does not treat them as hard constraints that force FK-invalid values.

issues.evidence: The NULL rule is implemented via _apply_null_rule driven by spec.NULL_TARGETS, with ALL_NULL_COLUMNS for Courses.other_details. This matches the interface rule (NULL share from compact, at least one NULL per nullable column, NOT NULL/PK/FK never NULL). However, because no instance was written, the NULL behavior could not be verified in execution. Also, _apply_null_rule computes share from schema.original_values, which may be a sampled subset — the share is still an estimate of the compact share, which is acceptable, but should be confirmed once instances are produced.
issues.requested_revision: After the FK fix, verify per-column NULL shares against the compact DB and confirm at least one NULL per nullable column and zero NULLs in NOT NULL/PK/FK columns. Report the 'generated rows: NULL 0 / n' lines for any nullable column that received no NULL.

issues.evidence: The group-size target (_apply_group_size_target) reserves indices 0..5 and assigns course ids c1 (size 1), c2 (size 2), c3 (size 3). But it picks c1,c2,c3 from the distinct values already in cols[course_id], which were FK-filled from the Courses pool. If the Courses pool has fewer than 3 distinct values (e.g. after CAST coercion collapses values, or if the pool is small), the target silently returns without applying. Also, the reserved indices may be overwritten by later _apply_semantic_rules or _apply_null_rule? No — those do not touch course_id (it is a FK, excluded from NULL rule; semantic rules do not touch it). But the group-size target runs before _apply_tie_target and _apply_different_values_target, which do not touch course_id. So the reservation is safe, provided >= 3 distinct course ids exist.
issues.requested_revision: Assert that at least 3 distinct course ids are available before applying the group-size target, and fail loudly (or log) if not, rather than silently skipping. Confirm the target is actually achieved in written instances.

issues.evidence: The tie target (_apply_tie_target) sets cols[date_of_attendance][1] to a fixed '09:00:00' on the same date as row 0. But row 0 and row 1 may have the same (student_id, course_id) composite PK, in which case the PK dedup in _finalize_table (sample_fresh_primary_keys) will drop one of them, destroying the tie. The spec note itself warns 'ensure ties survive dedup since PK includes both FK cols'. The code does not check that rows 0 and 1 have distinct (student_id,course_id).
issues.requested_revision: Before setting the tie, verify that rows 0 and 1 have distinct (student_id, course_id) tuples; if not, search for a pair of rows with distinct composite keys and set the tie on those. Add an assertion that the tie survives finalization.

issues.evidence: The different-values target (_apply_different_values_target) groups by candidate_id and sets assessment_date to base + k days for k>=1. But Candidate_Assessments PK is (candidate_id, qualification), and qualification is drawn from {A,B,C,D}. If a candidate has >= 2 rows but they share the same qualification, the PK dedup will drop one, potentially leaving only one row per candidate and defeating the target. The code does not ensure distinct qualifications within a candidate group.
issues.requested_revision: Ensure that within each candidate group, the qualification values are distinct (or that the target is applied only to groups that will survive PK dedup). Add an assertion that at least one candidate has >= 2 rows with different assessment_date values after finalization.

issues.evidence: The writer copies the compact DB and appends rows, but does not verify that the compact DB itself passes foreign_key_check before appending. If the compact DB has pre-existing FK violations (e.g. Student_Course_Attendance rows referencing registrations not present, or People_Addresses referencing missing addresses), the final foreign_key_check will fail regardless of generated rows. The 6-14 violations per instance are suspiciously stable, consistent with a fixed set of compact-DB violations plus a few generated ones.
issues.requested_revision: Run PRAGMA foreign_key_check on the copied compact DB before appending generated rows, and log the result. If the compact DB has violations, the specification's 'preserve compact rows' rule conflicts with the 'reject on any FK violation' rule; the designer must decide whether to (a) exclude the compact DB's violating rows, (b) relax the gate to only check generated rows, or (c) accept that the compact DB is the ground truth and only check that generated rows do not add new violations. This is a design decision that must be resolved before the engineer can make the gate pass.
